mechanism_narrative: A higher federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 3.0% indicates restrictive monetary policy that increases equity discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of economic regime.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 3.0%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.0% signals a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE is below 5.0%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in FEDFUNDS and rise in INDPRO signals monetary easing coupled with strong supply conditions, jointly driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (FEDFUNDS decline and INDPRO rise) produces positive 20-day returns in less than 40% of instances, or the interaction term Rank IC over any 3-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, housing starts (HOUST) below 2000.0 thousand units signal reduced consumer spending and business investment, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 2000.0 and FEDFUNDS > 3.5%, or the regime-specific Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption (RSAFS) over the past 6 months indicates robust consumer demand that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS is rising, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 100,000 signals strong labor market conditions that boost near-term consumer spending, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS increases by >100,000, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 115.0 indicates weakening manufacturing activity that reduces corporate profit visibility, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO is below 115.0, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 200.0 indicates persistent inflation that triggers aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of economic conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 200.0, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
